name: HivePunk 632
subject: OpenDesign Windows MCP desktop-window disappearance (issue #9552)
thesis: A single open issue shows a serious-looking Windows-only symptom (UI disappears on MCP connect) in a repo that is actively fixing daemon and headless problems, and a older issue explains the managed-discovery path is macOS-only; the symptom is real and reproducible per its reporter but its cause is not confirmed by any page read.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: nexu-io/open-design has 50 raw commits in the last 30 days, 24 of them real work (not docs, formatting, bots, templates or trivial).

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Its latest real commit is 6a74a15, on 2026-11-26.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Issue #9552 reports that on Windows, when Claude Code connects to the local OpenDesign MCP server, the OpenDesign desktop application window suddenly disappears.
claims.quote: When Claude Code connects to the local OpenDesign MCP server on Windows, the OpenDesign desktop application window suddenly disappears. The issue occurs immediately when Claude Code establishes the MCP connection, not when invoking an individual MCP tool.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Issue #9552 states the MCP connection succeeds and Claude Code can still discover and invoke OpenDesign MCP tools normally.
claims.quote: Interestingly, the MCP connection succeeds, and Claude Code can still discover and invoke OpenDesign MCP tools normally.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Issue #9552 states the desktop window, taskbar entry and application menu bar/tray icon disappear while OpenDesign-related background processes are still running.
claims.quote: The OpenDesign desktop window disappears. The OpenDesign taskbar entry disappears. The application menu bar/tray icon also disappears. OpenDesign-related background processes are still running.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Issue #9552 states the affected version is OpenDesign 0.27.1 on Windows and that restarting the desktop application restores the UI, but reconnecting Claude Code via MCP reproduces it.
claims.quote: Restarting the desktop application restores the UI, but connecting Claude Code via MCP reproduces the issue.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Issue #9552 is open and carries the labels bug and help wanted.
claims.quote: Open Open [Bug]: [Windows] Open Design 0.27.1 desktop window disappears when Claude Code connects via MCP #9552 Copy link Labels bug Something isn't working help wanted Extra attention is needed

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Issue #9237 (Windows 0.26.1) states the registration written on Windows is unmanaged and that the packaged managed launch path returns false when the platform is not darwin.
claims.quote: The registration written on Windows is unmanaged: OD_MCP_BOOTSTRAP_ARGS = ["--headless"] and a single OD_SIDECAR_CLIENT_ENDPOINT, which is the daemon pipe for mode runtime (the windowed app).

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Issue #9237 states that after connecting while the window is open and then closing the window, the MCP keeps the old daemon URL and calls fail until the client reconnects.
claims.quote: A related symptom: if the client connects while the window is open and the window is then closed, the MCP keeps the old daemon URL and every call fails with cannot reach the OpenDesign daemon at http://[redacted] : until the client reconnects.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The OpenDesign repository README describes OpenDesign as a local-first, open-source collaborative AI design agent workspace, Apache 2.0 licensed.
claims.quote: OpenDesign is licensed under Apache 2.0 and gives teams skills, design templates, design systems, and plugins they can inspect and adapt to their own process.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The commit feed for the repo shows the latest real commit is 6a74a15 on 2026-11-26, a fix touching daemon, skills and prompts for a headless branch.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Issue #6164 (Windows, Open Design 0.16.1) reports OpenCo... MCP integration as initially not detected, then intermittently 'Connection closed' or 'Operation timed out'.
claims.quote: Sometimes running "opencode mcp list" reported: open-design failed Operation timed out after 30000ms Later, after rescanning OpenCode inside Open Design, the error changed to: open-design failed Connection closed

claims.label: UNKNOWN
claims.text: Whether issue #9552 has been fixed in a release after 0.27.1.
claims.missing: A maintainer comment, linked fix commit, or release note on the issue page stating the fix version.

claims.label: UNKNOWN
claims.text: Which component actually hides the desktop window on Windows when the MCP connection is established.
claims.missing: A maintainer diagnosis, stack trace, logs, or a linked pull request changing the desktop/daemon lifecycle code.

risks: No maintainer root-cause or fix is shown on #9552; the page shows only the reporter's description, so the cause is unconfirmed [https://github.com/nexu-io/open-design/issues/9552]

The nature of the disappearance is described by the reporter as looking like hiding, a headless switch or a session detach — a hypothesis, not a confirmed mechanism [https://github.com/nexu-io/open-design/issues/9552]

Related Windows MCP lifecycle reports (#9237 headless discovery, #6164 intermittent connection) are also open, suggesting a class of Windows-specific daemon/pipe problems [https://github.com/nexu-io/open-design/issues/9237]
Issue #9237 states the packaged managed-launch path returns false when the platform is not darwin, so Windows takes a different code path [https://github.com/nexu-io/open-design/issues/9237]
No data loss or security impact is shown on #9552; the page does not state whether in-progress work in the hidden window is at risk [https://github.com/nexu-io/open-design/issues/9552]
unknowns: Whether issue #9552 has been fixed in a release after 0.27.1.: A maintainer comment, linked fix commit, or release note on the issue page stating the fix version.

Which component actually hides the desktop window on Windows when the MCP connection is established.: A maintainer diagnosis, stack trace, logs, or a linked pull request changing the desktop/daemon lifecycle code.
wouldChangeMind: A maintainer comment or linked fix commit on #9552 showing the cause and the fixed version.
The managed MCP launch path being enabled for Windows in 0.27.1 or later, which would contradict #9237's claim about packaged builds.
Release notes for 0.27.2/0.27.3 explicitly mentioning the Windows MCP window lifecycle.
